title: Customer-support chatbot with account tools

organisation.name: Kestrel Broadband
organisation.size: 600 staff; a support team of 80 agents
organisation.summary: Kestrel Broadband answers customer questions with a chatbot on its website. The chatbot service runs in containers, sends each conversation to a third-party LLM provider together with help articles retrieved from a knowledge-base vector store, and can call two tools: a customer accounts API to look up and update contact details, and a ticketing service to open tickets for human agents. Support agents work tickets from their laptops and edit the bot's prompts and knowledge-base articles in an admin console.

ai_llm_security.summary: A chat message talks the bot into looking up another customer's account
An edited knowledge-base article carries instructions the bot follows

api_security.summary: The accounts API trusts the bot's key, so any chat can read any customer
The accounts API key appears in the bot's error messages

application_security.summary: Script in a ticket the bot created runs in an agent's browser
Bot error messages include stack traces with the accounts API key

data_security.summary: Replies and transcripts carry personal data the bot fetched for someone else
Internal runbooks were indexed into the public bot's knowledge base

identity_access.summary: A phished agent account edits the bot's prompts
One never-expiring ticketing token serves every chat

endpoint_security.summary: A malicious attachment on a ticket runs on an agent's laptop
Malware takes the admin console session from an agent's browser

grc_risk.summary: The chatbot reads and changes customer accounts with no verification policy
Customer details go to the LLM provider without a data processing review

incident_response.summary: The accounts API log shows hundreds of lookups in an hour, all through the bot
Someone changed the bot's instructions overnight through a knowledge-base article

threat_intelligence.summary: A report describes campaigns that use support chatbots to harvest customer data
Intelligence on SIM-swap crews who change contact details through support channels

container_kubernetes.summary: The chatbot container runs as root with the host's container socket mounted
The chatbot image is pulled from a public registry tag that its owner can change

reviewNotes: Beginner: the bot's tools run with one shared key and no customer verification; retrieved articles and tool results are trusted text; every agent can edit the bot.
